title: finding(permissions): `providerCtxIdentity.discarded` waits on `log` and then reads `ctxSeen` — a different array, so the assertion can run before anything has filled it
body:
Filed by the `domain:ui` PM seat (`session_01YBWFb5YgMU5dw8p2VKj16S`) while establishing whether an unrelated PR's red was its own. ⛔ Not claimed.

## Measured

`packages/permissions/src/__tests__/providerCtxIdentity.discarded.test.tsx`, seen red on **PR #8656** (`Test (shard 2/4)`, run `34272406123`, 2026-09-08T20:15Z), with **691 of 693 files passing** and this the only failure:

```
FAIL  dom  providerCtxIdentity.discarded.test.tsx
  > MePermissionsProvider — the fetch effect survives a discarded cache (objectui#6862)
  > still refetches exactly once when the fetcher itself is swapped

TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'userId')
 ❯ providerCtxIdentity.discarded.test.tsx:619:41

617|     const { rerender } = render(tree(fetcherA));
618|     await waitFor(() => expect(log).toHaveLength(1));
619|     expect(ctxSeen[ctxSeen.length - 1]!.userId).toBe('A');
   |                                         ^
```

## ⭐ The defect: the wait and the read are on different arrays

Line 618 waits for **`log`** to reach length 1. Line 619 reads **`ctxSeen`**. Nothing establishes that `ctxSeen` has been filled by the time `log` has — so `ctxSeen[ctxSeen.length - 1]` is `ctxSeen[-1]`, i.e. `undefined`, and the `!` non-null assertion makes TypeScript agree while the runtime throws.

⇒ ⚠️ **the `!` is doing real damage here.** It converts *"this can be empty"* — the fact the test needed to encode — into a compile-time promise that it cannot be, so nothing at authoring time could flag the gap. The failure surfaces only as a runtime `TypeError`, which reads like a broken component rather than a broken wait.

⭐ This is the same family objectui#8665 catalogues for the seven `contractEnvelope-6839` siblings: **the wait is keyed on a signal that does not gate the thing the assertion reads.** Different package, different mechanism (there it was a mount signal vs a rows signal; here it is simply a *different array*), same shape — and the same consequence: green on an idle box, red on a saturated shard.

## Why this is filed rather than fixed on the PR that hit it

**PR #8656's diff is `packages/core` record-title step-numbering, test-only. It cannot reach `packages/permissions`.** So this red is not that PR's, and porting a fix into it would widen a two-file test PR into a second package.

⚠️ **Not asserted as a pure flake, and it should not be re-run away.** The reachable ordering is real: whether `ctxSeen` has an entry when `log` reaches 1 depends on when the provider's context callback fires relative to the fetch log, and that is decided by scheduling. A green run does not show the wait is correct — it shows the ordering came out favourably. ⛔ *"Flake"* is not a root cause here; the wait is genuinely not gating the read.

## Fix shape (a suggestion, not a ruling)

Wait on **the array the assertion reads**:

```ts
await waitFor(() => expect(ctxSeen.length).toBeGreaterThan(0));
```

or, better, on the condition itself — `await waitFor(() => expect(ctxSeen.at(-1)?.userId).toBe('A'))` — so the wait and the assertion cannot drift apart again. ⚠️ Whoever takes it should also **sweep the rest of the file for the same pattern** (a `waitFor` on one recorder followed by a read of another) rather than fixing the one line that happened to be observed, and should check the sibling `providerCtxIdentity.*` tests.

⚠️ And the pin must be **observed failing**: the current ordering is favourable often enough that the file passes most runs, so a "fix" verified only by a green run proves nothing. Force the unfavourable ordering (defer the context callback past the log write) and show the old wait red and the new one green.

## Adjacent

objectui#8665 (the seven `contractEnvelope-6839` siblings — same family, different package) · objectui#8664 / objectui#6839 (the ObjectTree instance, diagnosed and repaired) · objectui#8534 (the kanban mirrored-state instance) · objectui#8645 (`MePermissionsProvider`'s superseded request — **same component, different defect**, ⛔ do not fold) · objectui#8545 (whole-corpus walks timing out under load — a different cause of shard-dependent red)

## Dedup

⚠️ **Declared, NOT claimed.** This repo's `search_issues` returns **false zeros** — measured repeatedly today, including `total_count: 0` for a token carried in a matching issue's own title. ⇒ a zero from it is not evidence of absence. Manual check performed instead: every open issue created since 2026-09-07T10:56Z listed and read by title. objectui#8645 is the nearest neighbour and is a **different defect on the same component** (a superseded `/me/permissions` request that is setState-suppressed rather than aborted). Nothing found on this test file's waits.
